newsitem.title: USA: State Dept confirms Israel role on Hebron.
newsitem.headline: State Dept confirms Israel role on Hebron.

text.p: The State Department backed up its envoys in confirming on Wednesday that Israel would decide the depth of three future troop redeployments in the just-signed Hebron agreement.

"The letters of assurance which Secretary (of State Warren) Christopher intends to provide to both parties also refers to the process of further redeployments as an Israeli responsibility, which includes its (Israel) designating specified military locations," spokesman Nicholas Burns said in a statement.

Also, a "note for the record, prepared by the United States at the request of the parties, makes clear that further redeployment phases are issues for implementation by Israel rather than issues for negotiation with the Palestinians," Burns said.
The statement was issued as an Israeli spokesman announced that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet accepted Israel's Hebron deal with the Palestinians by a vote of 11-7.
Netanyahu earlier interrupted a stormy cabinet debate on the Hebron accord to check a TV report seized on by hardliners as a reason to scupper the deal, which was later rectracted.

The report on Israel's Channel One Television quoted a State Department spokesman as saying Israel would not on its own decide how much future West Bank land it would give Palestinians -- but would have to negotiate the issue with the PLO. The report was dismissed by the State Department, and later retracted by Israel Television's Washington reporter.
